steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Dance appreciation is the ability to analyse, describe and evaluate dance works using informed judgement

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The AO4 framework is the AQA assessment objective for appreciation: analyse and evaluate dance

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Analysis means breaking down a dance into its component parts to understand how it works

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Description involves identifying and clearly stating what you see in a dance performance

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What does AO4 assess in GCSE Dance? | Q: Explain the difference between describing and analysing a dance. | Q: Why must evaluation be supported by evidence?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: AO4 assesses the ability to analyse and evaluate dance, including professional works and own choreographic practice. | Describing means stating what you see (e.g. 'the dancers move in unison'); analysing means explaining how and why it works (e.g. 'unison creates a sense of unity reinforcing the choreographic intent') | Without evidence, evaluation is just opinion. AQA requires informed judgements backed by specific examples from the dance to show understanding.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always structure appreciation answers in order: describe, analyse, evaluate — it keeps your response logical and complete Use subject-specific terminology such as 'unison', 'canon', 'sustained dynamics' rather than everyday language In evaluation, always justify your judgement with a specific example from the dance Link every point back to the choreographic intention — AQA marks answers that connect analysis to purpose AO4 is 40% of the written exam, so practise timed appreciation responses regularly
